title: Inspect and export companies and opportunities
summary: Read accepted current companies, opportunities, and source metadata. Export the existing consistent JSON snapshot for downstream selection. Milieu performs no collection.
use_when: A caller needs accepted current company/opportunity records, supplied evidence, or source metadata.
A downstream product needs a consistent machine-readable discovery snapshot.
do_not_use_when: Current remote sources must be fetched; Milieu no longer provides collection.
The caller needs a personal recommendation or application workflow.
outcome: Stored company/opportunity records or one consistent schema-one snapshot carrying stable identities, current revisions, compatibility fields, supplied evidence, and source metadata.
effects: Read supported Milieu state without fetching external sources or running a model. Output may disclose private posting text, evidence, dates, and source locators.
An explicit export --output writes and atomically replaces a private caller-selected file; stdout reads do not write an export.
authority: Milieu owns stored company and opportunity identities, revisions, source metadata and read projections.
Consumers own filtering, consumed revisions, packet state and notification history.
success: The requested read completes against supported initialized state. Export returns a consistent snapshot with schema version, revision, capture time, companies, opportunities, source metadata and an empty query coverage array.
failure_and_recovery: An empty result contains no stored records matching the selected query and limits.
Reads do not refresh information. Milieu has no collection interface. Read milieu.state for supported storage, local readiness, and recovery. Do not inspect or repair SQLite directly.
privacy: CLI output and exported snapshots are private caller-owned data. Reads send no information to remote systems.
does_not_authorize: Selecting opportunities for the user, creating CRM cases or application packets, sending email, submitting applications, invoking an agent or browser, or enabling a schedule.
Fetching sources during a read operation.

consumers.statement: Local callers and downstream products can inspect accepted current records and consume the existing consistent export and provider-owned Rust read types.

preconditions.statement: The selected state directory contains a supported initialized Milieu database and the requested identity or command is valid.

inputs.statement: Inputs are one selected state directory, a supported read command and optional record identity.

outputs.statement: CLI record reads use readable text by default. Global --json selects existing machine schemas. JSON list/search return schema-two pages with snapshot_revision, compact items and has_more. The default limit is 20; --limit accepts a positive integer. Opportunity rows contain stable ID and revision, company, title, location, remote eligibility, recorded availability and last_seen_at. Search adds matched_field and a marked excerpt of at most 240 Unicode characters. Show and export return full records and source metadata. The export snapshot uses schema 1. Export --output always writes JSON; --json selects only its stdout receipt format. Operational errors exit 1: text on stderr by default, or schema-one ok:false with error.detail on stderr with --json. Syntax errors remain Clap text on stderr with exit 2. Local status and doctor belong to milieu.state. The native Rust Snapshot handoff remains unchanged.

data_semantics.statement: Reads and exports include all retained opportunities without a title substring requirement. Opportunity counts describe retained records rather than all external postings. Consumers choose opportunities by title, seniority, location or other preferences.

An opportunity employer exports as company_id, independently of an optional source operator. Compatibility metadata preserves supplied dates, evidence, compensation and other exported fields without observation or revision history. Company/opportunity first_seen_at and last_seen_at normalize to UTC with nine fractional-second digits. Entity revisions use exported material fields excluding last_seen_at. Secondary appearances and hybrid/on-site changes can preserve the export revision while advancing snapshot_revision.

Accepted descriptions are stored as supplied. Status accepts unknown, listed, unlisted, missing or presumed_closed and projects to availability. These values are accepted assertions; they establish no fresh observation. Supplied attribution, missing-scan counts, first absence times, parser versions, fingerprints and source dates remain compatibility evidence. Milieu does not scan or calculate availability.

Opportunities store multiple source appearances but export one caller-selected primary through source_id, source_key and url. That tuple remains fixed after creation; adding secondary appearances preserves it. Consumers retain the primary URL and optional apply_url. Secondary appearance URLs are not added to this interface. Workplaces export comma-separated names in location-ID order, or null. Remote work_mode exports remote:true; hybrid and on-site export remote:false; absent work_mode exports null. Other values are rejected.

The exported source company_id is a compatibility association distinct from source operator and opportunity employer. Source enabled, status, timestamps, cursor and note remain supplied metadata; no collector acts on them.

identity_and_units.statement: Company, opportunity and source IDs are opaque stable Milieu identities. Source-native IDs are scoped to their source namespace. Company identity aliases remain retained. A snapshot revision identifies stored state at export. Matching names alone do not merge companies.
Reads define no billing or physical unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Export is one consistent view of all stored companies and opportunities and projected source metadata. The coverage array is empty because current state has no query coverage or collection history. source_health retains its existing field name and carries source metadata. captured_at describes capture time; record dates describe supplied compatibility evidence.

Read operations return stored records without fetching source URLs. Milieu has no collection commands. Supported storage is defined by milieu.state; the public Snapshot and schema-one export remain the consumer handoff.

access.statement: Supported consumers use the local CLI or the provider-owned Rust read surface milieu::store::Store::open and Store::snapshot, returning milieu::models::Snapshot. Direct SQLite is not a consumer boundary.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: A snapshot reads within one database transaction and starts no collection work. Separate reads need not share a snapshot.

operational_limits.statement: The export returns retained current records rather than a durable event stream or consumer acknowledgement protocol.
No maximum database size, export size or read-latency service level is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Read contract 3 preserves the export/native Snapshot and record-read consumer boundary. Export schema 1 and list/search schema 2 are independent of the Milieu package and database versions. Milieu 0.6.0 local CLI and storage retirements are declared by state contract 3.
No future deprecation window is promised.

Canonical commands use opportunities and opportunity, with hidden jobs and job aliases accepting the same arguments. Human output uses opportunity terminology. JSON retains jobs and kind:job, and public Rust Job types and database names remain unchanged. No state migration is required.

reliances.statement: Reads use only Milieu retained local state. Source locators are stored evidence and cause no remote call.
